svg.text: Where the agent information lives, and how it reaches the marketplace
BigQuery is the system of record. Only the backend has a data path; the frontend holds no durable copy and no credential.
Three, and only three, ways a row enters or changes in the catalogue. Every one lands in the same table and leaves the same audit record.
What happens on a page load, and what happens when somebody votes.
the user sees it at once
The application never reads a row, changes
it and writes it back. A vote is an event;
the count is a view over those events. Any
number of Cloud Run instances can accept
votes at the same moment without a lock and
without losing one. It is also why the count
Rejected: Firestore for hot state with
BigQuery as an analytics sink. Faster on
paper, but it splits the system of record
across two stores with two access models,
two retention mechanisms and two lineage
stories. If read latency ever binds, add a
cache in front of BigQuery, not a second
Why BigQuery is fast enough to serve a UI
A few hundred catalogue rows, cached 300
seconds, so at most twelve round trips an
hour per instance. Cost is immaterial and
p95 render stays inside the 1.5 second
budget. BI Engine is there if the budget
